title: Tex Mex Baked Chicken
conventions: buy strings are cook measures (what goes in the pot). Grams are TARGET-scale: the mapper states them where its printed measure quantizes away from the exact scale, and otherwise they are parse-compute's source-basis weight for that line multiplied by scale_factor exactly once.

ingredients.notes: COST BASIS WARNING: 510 g is the DRAINED weight that goes in the dish (about 255 g per 15 oz can), which is the right basis for macros against the 1/2 cup = 130 g drained label. The purchase is 30 oz gross per source batch, so a per-gram cost off this number under-prices the cans by roughly 40%. The line names its own form - 2 15-oz cans, drained - so this is canned, not dry, and plain rather than the Seasoned Black Beans row. Grams are the drained yield (255 g per can), matching the food row's drained 1/2 cup = 130 g basis.

House medium onion, same 110 g the table used for the red onion in the sister recipe. Same form, same variety as the Yellow Onion vocabulary row; onions is priced 7 of 7. Not red-onion, which is its own variety price.

119 g is the existing Green Bell Peppers food row's own medium-pepper each-weight. Green is a separate price class from red by standing precedent and the estate already carries red and yellow as their own ids; no commodity claims green, so the id is proposed rather than bridged. canon_item uses the plural spelling deliberately - it is the exact existing food-macros-db row (24 cal / 119 g).
Weight stated on the line. Plain breasts, weight stated on the line; chicken-breast priced 7 of 7. Note 1 is a thickness note, not a cut change.

USDA chili powder 2.7 g per tsp. The source's own step 1 calls this line chili powder, and 1/2 tsp is a spice-jar measure, not a seasoning packet. Same spice-aisle product and price class; existing Chili Powder food row.

240 g per cup, matching the Enchilada Sauce row's 1/4 cup = 60 g label. Red is the default the enchilada-sauce commodity prices (5 of 7 stores) and the Enchilada Sauce food row is Old El Paso red; 'red' is a qualifier here, not a form flip.
Settled identity but the table computed NO weight, so I weighed it: 1/4 cup shredded = 28 g on the Cheddar Cheese, Shredded row, so 1 1/2 cups = 170 g.

ingredients.source_raw: 1/2 cup crumbled cotija cheese (or queso fresco)
ingredients.notes: 1 oz = 28 g is about 1/4 cup crumbled on the Cacique label. Board ABSENT: no commodity and no capture match. Will not bridge onto parmesan or a generic cheese id - different food, different price class - so null with the term enqueued. New label row added.

No quantity on the source page; 10 g source is a garnish handful and is macro-immaterial. A chopped garnish is fresh cilantro, not dried coriander leaf; the cilantro commodity is priced 6 of 7 and the Fresh Cilantro food row exists. The extraction marks the line optional.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Standing precedent explicitly rejects pricing green peppers off red-bell-pepper (variety price class), and the estate already splits this food by colour: red-bell-pepper and yellow-bell-pepper are separate ids and separate food-DB rows (31 vs 27 cal per 100 g), with a Green Bell Peppers macro row already on the books at 24 cal / 119 g. The pre-resolve's own namespace sweep returned 'no commodity claims it' while today's captures carry matching products, so this is an unpriced sibling of two existing ids rather than a duplicate of any of them. If a green-pepper id already exists under another spelling, alias to it - the food is the ordinary fresh green bell pepper, sold by the each.

registrar_rulings.reason: The id already exists and is already priced - the mapper's sweep missed the recipe-board namespace: recipe-board-everyday.json carries a 'green-bell-pepper' row (Green Bell Pepper, unit=each, fresh green bells at Sam's/Walmart/Aldi/Baker's, e.g. 'Fresh Green Bell Pepper' $0.86), the live feed smp-feed.json prices green-bell-pepper at $0.77/each (Fareway, n=5 stores), and recipe-floor-id-map.json already declares the recipe-spelling alias green-bell-pepper -> bell-peppers (the weekly staples id whose include patterns cover 'green\s+bell' and which shows the identical $0.77 Fareway crown, n=5 - the same rows). Nothing to mint and no edit needed: resolve the tex-mex-baked-chicken line to the existing green-bell-pepper id (per-each), which the existing floor-map entry already routes to the bell-peppers weekly commodity.

macro_cross_check.verdict: PASS ON PROTEIN (+11.3%, inside the band, so the 907 g chicken and the cheese portions are right) but FLAG THE CARBS LOUDLY. The source's published 16 g carb per serving is arithmetically impossible with two 15-oz cans of black beans: 510 g drained carries 86 g of carbohydrate on its own, which is 21.6 g per serving before anything else on the line list. Our 32.3 g is the honest number and the source's is wrong, most likely a net-carb or one-can calculation. Two consequences the orchestrator should see: at 32.3 g this recipe still clears the run's 35 g ceiling, but only by 2.7 g, and at 637 cal it clears the 650 ceiling by 13 - both would flip if the beans were costed at gross can weight instead of drained, or if the cheese were rounded up.
